greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Grace and peace be with you all as we gather around the Word of the Lord.
penitential:
Lord, you search our hearts and know our deepest longings; Lord, have mercy.
Christ, you teach us the way of humility and true grace; Christ, have mercy.
Lord, you are the living water that quenches our deepest thirst; Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: My soul is thirsting for the living God.
homily:
We begin today not with a grand theological argument or a complicated doctrine, but with something very small, quiet, and ordinary. Think of a traveler standing at a crossroads, carrying a map, looking up at the sky to see which way the wind is blowing. Or think of someone waking up before the sun is fully over the rooftops, pausing in the quiet hallway of a home, listening to the morning settle around them. There is a moment in every day when we realize that we are on a journey, that we are moving from one place to another, and that the ground beneath our feet is only temporary. We are all travelers here. We are all looking for a horizon that does not fade.

I want you to hold onto that single image: the traveler at the crossroads, looking up at the sky and feeling the pull of a destination far beyond this earth.

Now, let us tell the truth before we try to comfort ourselves. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you gathered here or listening from afar with heavy hearts: we know what it is like to stand in a room that feels too still. It has been four months since Benjamin Vo went home to God, and the silence in your home does not ask for polite platitudes. It asks for honesty. You look at the places where he used to be—the desk where he coded his games, the bright, curious spaces he filled with his brilliant mind and his gentle spirit—and the weight of missing him is real. It is a heavy ache. It is an ache that makes the world feel vast and empty all at once. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to miss him with every breath you take. You are allowed to be human.

There is a temptation, when we carry such a deep sorrow, to look back over the years and wonder if we missed something, if we could have done more, if some small detail slipped through our hands. Let us lift that stone from your hearts right now. You missed nothing. You were the parents and the brother that Benjamin was given. You loved him with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with wonder, with travel across the world, with shared stories and laughter. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. Some sorrows in this fragile world arrive untouched by anything anyone did or failed to do. You are not to blame. Let that heavy stone fall to the ground, and let your shoulders rest.

Right into the middle of that ache, the Word of God breaks in like light coming under a closed door. Listen to the Apostle Paul speaking from a Roman prison in our first reading today. He says: 'For to me life is Christ, and death is gain. If I go on living in the flesh, that means fruitful labor for me. And I do not know which I shall choose. I am caught between the two. I long to depart this life and be with Christ, for that is far better.' Think of what Paul is saying. He is looking at life and death not with terror, but with a profound, steady clarity. He sees that earthly life is a place of labor, of love, of serving one another, but he also knows that the ultimate horizon is Christ. He is caught between two loves: the love for those he is serving here, and the longing for the One who is waiting for him there.

Benjamin was a boy who understood horizons. Think of his brilliant, searching mind—a mind that mastered mathematics years ahead of his time, that dived into the complexities of cloud infrastructure, and that looked at the vastness of the sky with a boundless passion for aviation. He loved the mechanics of flight, the pure joy of soaring high above the clouds. He even dreamed of creating his own airline, 'con chim airlines,' talking about it with that wonderful, infectious giggle that brought a smile to everyone around him. He was a boy who looked at the sky and saw invitation, not limitation. He had a heart that was remarkably generous. Think of how, at just fifteen years old, he offered his entire piggy bank, unprompted, to help an uncle who was suffering. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent, beautiful soul God had placed inside him. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who walked beside you on your journeys.

And now, Benjamin is soaring. He is at the banquet of heaven, resting in the light of the Father. He is home.

Look at the Gospel we heard just a moment ago. Jesus goes to dine at the home of a Pharisee, and he notices how the guests are scrambling for the places of honor at the table. They are trying to elevate themselves, to prove their worth, to secure their status in the eyes of the world. But Jesus tells them a better way. He speaks of taking the lowest place, of humility, of letting the host come and say, 'My friend, move up to a higher position.' Jesus is turning our human calculations upside down. He is showing us that true greatness is not found in pushing ourselves forward, but in the quiet grace of a heart that receives everything as a gift from God.

Benjamin lived that gentle humility. He was brilliant, yet he was deeply respectful, sweet, and effortlessly happy. He didn't need the places of honor; he just wanted to share his smile, his curiosity, and his love with his family—his 'perfect four' of Dad, Mom, and Ryan. And now, the Host of heaven has approached him and said, 'My friend, move up to a higher position.' He is resting in the highest place of all, wrapped in the eternal embrace of God.

Alan, Thao, Ryan, when you feel the quiet of the house, remember that love does not end at the grave. You are still a family of four. Death cannot sever what God has joined together. When you look at the sky, when you think of the planes, when you remember the simple, everyday joys you shared, know that Benjamin is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. Think of the clean water flowing in Cà Mau, Vietnam, from the well dedicated in his name—the 'Great Ocean' of his middle name poured out to quench the thirst of the poor. His love did not stop when his breathing stopped. It keeps moving. It keeps giving. It keeps blessing the earth.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a holy, beautiful legacy. You know the games you coded together, the laughter you shared, the simple life of being brothers. You are not walking this path alone. Carry his joy with you. Keep being the boy who looks at the world with curiosity and an open heart. You are a vital part of this family, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing in the universe.

So what do you carry out the door today? Not a heavy burden, not an impossible set of answers, but one small, doable thing: when the day feels long and the house feels quiet, pause for a moment. Look up at the sky. Imagine the vast horizon that Benjamin loved so much. Let yourself feel the quiet assurance that he is completely at peace, waiting for you in the light. Walk out into the world with the unshakeable hope that love is stronger than death, and that the story is not finished. You are held in the palm of God's hand, today and always. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ.
For Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all who carry the heavy weight of grief, that God console them, heal their hearts, and fill them with enduring hope.
For children who are suffering and for every family carrying a heavy cross, that they may feel the warm, protective embrace of our Lord.
For our community and for all who seek to live close to Jesus, to the Father, and to Our Lady Mary, that we may be instruments of His peace.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, wipe away every tear from your eyes, and bring you safely home to His eternal peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
As long as in every way, whether in pretense or in truth,
Christ is being proclaimed, and in that I rejoice.Indeed I shall continue to rejoice,
for I know that this will result in deliverance for me
through your prayers and support from the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
My eager expectation and hope
is that I shall not be put to shame in any way,
but that with all boldness, now as always,
Christ will be magnified in my body,
whether by life or by death.
For to me life is Christ, and death is gain.
If I go on living in the flesh, that means fruitful labor for me.
And I do not know which I shall choose.
I am caught between the two.
I long to depart this life and be with Christ,
for that is far better.
Yet that I remain in the flesh is more necessary for your benefit.
And this I know with confidence,
that I shall remain and continue in the service of all of you
for your progress and joy in the faith,
so that your boasting in Christ Jesus may abound on account of me
when I come to you again.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. My soul is thirsting for the living God.
As the hind longs for the running waters,
so my soul longs for you, O God.
R. My soul is thirsting for the living God.
Athirst is my soul for God, the living God.
When shall I go and behold the face of God?
R. My soul is thirsting for the living God.
I went with the throng
and led them in procession to the house of God.
Amid loud cries of joy and thanksgiving,
with the multitude keeping festival.
R. My soul is thirsting for the living God.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
On a sabbath Jesus went to dine
at the home of one of the leading Pharisees,
and the people there were observing him carefully.He told a parable to those who had been invited,
noticing how they were choosing the places of honor at the table.
“When you are invited by someone to a wedding banquet,
do not recline at table in the place of honor.
A more distinguished guest than you may have been invited by him,
and the host who invited both of you may approach you and say,
‘Give your place to this man,’
and then you would proceed with embarrassment
to take the lowest place.
Rather, when you are invited, 
go and take the lowest place
so that when the host comes to you he may say,
‘My friend, move up to a higher position.’
Then you will enjoy the esteem of your companions at the table.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled,
but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

day: Saturday of the Thirtieth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
